We instruct our chosen MLLM (GPT-4V or Gemini) to assess each claim's hallucinatory potential. In doing so, the MLLM also generates insightful explanations to elucidate the rationale behind its judgment.

We allocate the dataset uniformly across three annotators with graduate-level qualifications for independent categorization. Decisions in uncertain cases were initially held by individual annotators and later resolved by majority rule.
guideline: Our annotation criteria evaluate whether image-to-text output conflicts with the input image or world knowledge and whether text-to-image visuals conflict with claims or world knowledge.

Extracted claims are labeled as hallucinatory or nonhallucinatory, with a segment deemed hallucinatory if it contains any such claim; otherwise, it is labeled non-hallucinatory. An entire response is labeled hallucinatory if it includes even one hallucinatory segment.
